content.text:
I've read all six changed files and traced the data flow:

**page.tsx** — The join-to-two-queries refactor operates on `outfit_items` and `wear_logs`. Both tables have RLS enabled (per `20260718090000_outfits.sql`): `outfit_items_own` requires the parent outfit to be owned by `auth.uid()`, and `wear_logs_own` restricts to `user_id = auth.uid()`. The new pattern (`outfit_items.eq("item_id", itemId)` → `wear_logs.in("outfit_id", outfitIds)`) is protected end-to-end by RLS. No cross-tenant leak: even if `outfitIds` were somehow tainted, `wear_logs`'s own RLS returns only the caller's logs.

**style-actions.ts** — The cache key now derives from `profile.location_timezone` (user-controllable) instead of the forecast timezone. `loadStyledLook` is keyed by `(user.id, itemId, today)`, so a user manipulating their own timezone only affects their own cache namespace — no cross-user cache-poisoning or quota bypass (the cache lookup only returns a hit if a prior generation stored something under that key for this user; misses fall through to `assertCanGenerate`). An invalid TZ would throw, caught by the outer try/catch — same envelope as before.

**item-view.tsx / item-detail.tsx** — Pure presentation: tile styling, subtitle dedup logic (`item.subcategory === title ? null : item.subcategory`), and moving `StyleCta` construction into the client component. All user-derived values (`title`, subtitle) are rendered as React children/attributes and auto-escaped. `imageUrl` is a Supabase-signed URL, not user-controlled.

**Test files** — Additional vi.mock; no runtime impact.

No source→sink path with a missing mitigation is introduced by this diff.
